entries.identity: Kangying Zhou, Professional Investors and Media Topics, author PDF dated 2026-03-16
entries.relevant_hypothesis: Separate topic attention from textual sentiment and avoid using one as a proxy for the other.
entries.project_boundary: The pilot has a selected issuer-announcement subset and no complete media-attention denominator.

entries.identity: Zheng Tracy Ke, Bryan Kelly, Dacheng Xiu, Predicting Returns with Text Data, author conference PDF dated 2019-05-14
entries.relevant_hypothesis: Text may add information beyond generic sentiment and price controls, requiring an actually paired out-of-time comparison.
entries.project_boundary: This run does not borrow supervised term weights or its reported return results.

entries.identity: Steven L. Heston and Nitish R. Sinha, News versus Sentiment: Predicting Stock Returns from News Stories, Federal Reserve FEDS 2016-048
entries.relevant_hypothesis: The outcome horizon and source timestamp are material; distinct horizons must be reported separately.
entries.project_boundary: This pilot scores official disclosures and does not claim to replicate a newswire study.

entries.identity: Loughran-McDonald Master Dictionary, Notre Dame SRAF, observed March 2026 edition covering 1993-2025
entries.relevant_hypothesis: A fixed finance-specific positive-minus-negative term frequency can serve as a lexical tone baseline.
entries.project_boundary: Research-use terms apply; edition is not proven available on every 2025 signal date.

entries.identity: ProsusAI/finbert, official model card and repository
entries.relevant_hypothesis: A fixed English financial-language classifier can provide a separate textual tone measure.
entries.project_boundary: Scores are neither source-fact verification nor a probability of future stock returns.
